stem: A nurse used a respirator and other PPE while caring for a client in an airborne-infection isolation room. Which removal principle is correct when care is complete?

options.A: Keep all PPE on until reaching the nurses' station
options.B: Remove the respirator inside the room before removing contaminated gloves and gown
options.C: Remove other PPE before leaving the room or care area; remove the respirator after leaving and closing the door
options.D: Remove PPE in any order and location because hand hygiene eliminates doffing risk

rationale: CDC Core Infection Prevention Practices state that PPE other than respirators should be removed and discarded after the task and before leaving the patient's room or care area. If a respirator is used, it should be removed after leaving the room/care area and closing the door. C is correct.
educational_objective: Apply the CDC location/sequence principle for removing a respirator and other PPE after airborne-isolation care.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Safe Healthcare Delivery in All Settings
source_locator: Core Practices Table, 5d Risk Assessment with Appropriate Use of PPE, items 1.4-1.5; lines 111-120 on current page
source_claim_supported: PPE other than respirators is removed before leaving the patient's room/care area; respirators are removed after leaving and closing the door.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — transmission-based precautions and PPE
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — PPE doffing for airborne precautions

source_original.stem: A nurse is leaving an airborne-precaution room after completing care. Which PPE-removal principle is correct?

options.A: Keep all PPE on until reaching the nurses' station so every item can be removed at one location
options.B: Remove the respirator inside the patient room before removing contaminated gloves and gown
options.C: Remove other PPE before leaving the care area, then remove the respirator after exit and door closure
options.D: Remove PPE in any order or location because correct hand hygiene makes doffing sequence irrelevant

source_original.rationale: CDC core practices direct healthcare personnel to remove and discard PPE other than respirators before leaving the patient room or care area. A respirator is removed after leaving the room or care area and closing the door, with hand hygiene performed appropriately.
source_original.source_detail: CDC Core Infection Prevention Practices: remove non-respirator PPE before leaving care area; respirator after exit/door closure; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Retained the correct CDC doffing principle, added an exact Core Practices table locator, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the item tests a direct procedural standard rather than complex clinical judgment.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC Core Practices; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: CDC Core Practices current page checked 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.claim_audit: CDC explicitly distinguishes the removal location for respirators versus other PPE and requires door closure before respirator removal.

distractor_audit.A: Carries contaminated PPE beyond the care area.
distractor_audit.D: Hand hygiene does not make doffing location/sequence irrelevant.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: C is uniquely supported by CDC.
audit_findings.cueing: No answer cue beyond the relevant airborne-room context.
audit_findings.blueprint: Transmission-based precautions/PPE fit Safety and Infection Prevention and Control.
